title: Timeless Jewels Guide: Heroic Tragedy, Undying Hate, Seeds and Desecration Risk
summary: Timeless Jewels are a Unique jewel family in Path of Exile 2 0.5.4. Heroic Tragedy (Kalguur) drops from Olroth at Difficulty 4; Undying Hate (Abyssal) drops from Vessel of Kulemak. This guide covers the Seed/Keystone/Name system, how each jewel conquers passives in radius, Preserved Cranium and Unstable Desecration risk, the 0.4 Undying Hate keystone change, and a build-by-build usage breakdown.
description: How Timeless Jewels work in PoE2 0.5.4: Heroic Tragedy and Undying Hate seed/keystone mechanics, radius conquest, desecration risk, the 0.4 keystone change, and build usage.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Timeless Jewels family overview showing Heroic Tragedy and Undying Hate and their seed and keystone system

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Timeless Jewels are a family of Historic Unique jewels. Each is Limited to 1 per character, has a Very Large radius (1500), and conquers every small and notable passive in radius, replacing them with themed versions. Heroic Tragedy (Kalguur) drops from Olroth at Difficulty 4; Undying Hate (Abyssal) drops from Vessel of Kulemak. The seed number decides Notable outcomes and the jewel's name decides Keystone outcomes.
calloutDetail: A Timeless Jewel is NOT a Time-Lost Jewel - different item, different mechanic.
Seed (the number) decides what Notables in radius become; the name (leader/faction) decides what Keystones become.
Undying Hate can be Desecrated up to 4 times with Preserved Craniums, but Desecration makes it Unstable and raises the chance it is destroyed.

answers.label: Use for
text: Builds that want a specific Keystone conversion (Heroic Tragedy) or a Tribute-scaling Abyssal build (Undying Hate), and players willing to roll seeds for perfect Notables.

answers.label: Check first
text: Confirm the seed and name against a planner or the live client before buying; the same jewel name with a different seed is a completely different result.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Assuming old 0.1/0.2 conclusions still apply, and assuming a fixed desecration destruction percentage - only an increasing probability is officially described.

facts.label: Family

facts.label: Limited to

facts.label: Drop sources

sections.title: Family overview: the two members
intro: The Timeless Jewel family currently has two members. Both conquer passives in a Very Large radius but with completely different themes and drop sources.
Because only one Historic jewel is allowed per character, choosing between them (or between seeds of the same jewel) is a permanent build decision.

members.title: Heroic Tragedy
members.sub: Remembering (100-8000) songworthy deeds by the line of Vorana / Medved / Olroth
body: Conquers passives in radius for the Kalguur. Seed 100-8000 decides Notable outcomes; the leader name (Vorana, Medved, or Olroth) decides the Keystone the in-radius Keystones become. Drops from Olroth, Origin of the Fall at Expedition Difficulty 4.

members.title: Undying Hate
members.sub: Glorifying the defilement of (79-30977) souls in tribute to Amanamu / Ulaman / Kurgal / Tecrod / Kulemak
body: Conquers passives in radius for the Abyssals. Seed 79-30977 decides Notable outcomes; the faction name decides the Keystone. Small passives become Tribute; Notables scale with Tribute. Can be Desecrated up to 4 times with Preserved Craniums (Unstable Desecration). Drops from Vessel of Kulemak.

cells.heroic: Travel nodes gain Ward; other small nodes gain Ward
cells.undying: Small passives become Tribute (+5 each, +3 attribute Tribute)

cells.heroic: Transformed by seed into Kalguur notables
cells.undying: Transformed by seed into Tribute-scaling Abyssal notables
Preserved Cranium Desecration (up to 4) + Divine rerolls

sections.note: Both are Limited to 1 Historic and share the Very Large radius. The decisive difference is theme: Kalguur defensive attribute conversion (Heroic Tragedy) versus Abyssal Tribute scaling and Desecration (Undying Hate).

sections.title: Overview: how Timeless Jewels work
paragraphs: A Timeless Jewel is socketed into a normal allocated Jewel Socket. Every small and notable passive inside its Very Large radius is 'Conquered' and replaced with a themed version. Conquered nodes cannot be further modified by other radius jewels, so the choice of socket and seed is final for that build.

Two numbers drive the result. The seed (the random number on the jewel) deterministically decides what the Notable passives in radius become. The name (the leader for Heroic Tragedy, the faction for Undying Hate, shown at the end of the flavour line) decides what Keystones in radius become. A Divine Orb rerolls both the seed and the name.

Heroic Tragedy conquers for the Kalguur: each leader converts one attribute's inherent bonus into a defensive scaling (for example Strength into Energy Shield, Dexterity into Armour, Intelligence into Evasion depending on the leader), and seed 100-8000 picks the Notables. Undying Hate conquers for the Abyssals: small passives become Tribute, Notables scale with your total Tribute, and the faction name picks the Keystone (Sacrifice of Flesh/Sight/Mind/Blood/Loyalty).

Current versus legacy: the 0.4.0 patch changed Undying Hate's Tecrod 'Sacrifice of Blood' Keystone - it now grants 1 Life per second per 16 Life spent in the past 4 seconds and 20% more Life Cost of Skills (previously 8 Life per second per 8 Life spent, 50% more). Conclusions about Undying Hate keystones from 0.1 or 0.2 are invalid. There is no official PoE2 Timeless Jewel calculator yet, so verify seeds in Path of Building or the client before committing currency.
bullets: Timeless != Time-Lost: different item, different mechanic.
Limited to 1 Historic jewel per character.
Conquered nodes cannot be re-modified by other radius jewels.
Undying Hate: 0.4 changed Tecrod's Sacrifice of Blood; old conclusions invalid.

sections.note: The same jewel name with a different seed, or the same seed in a different socket, produces a different result. Verify all three fields (seed, name, socket) every time.

sections.title: Eligibility: what a Timeless Jewel affects
note: A Timeless Jewel only acts on nodes inside its radius and is blocked by the single-Historic limit. Nodes outside the radius and nodes already conquered by another Historic jewel are untouched.

sections.title: Desecration Risk (Unstable Desecration)
sections.caption: Undying Hate can be Desecrated up to 4 times. Official wording describes an INCREASING destruction probability - no fixed percentage is published. Treat the risk as rising with each use; do not rely on a fixed number.

sections.note: The only official statement is that Desecration makes the item Unstable and the destruction probability increases with use. Community sample estimates exist but are NOT official; this guide does not state a fixed destruction percentage.

sections.title: How to use a Timeless Jewel

steps.label: Acquire the jewel
body: Farm Olroth at Difficulty 4 for Heroic Tragedy, or Vessel of Kulemak for Undying Hate, or buy an identified copy on trade.

steps.label: Choose the socket
body: Place it in a normal allocated Jewel Socket whose Very Large radius covers the nodes you want conquered.

steps.label: Preview the seed
body: Load the seed into Path of Building or the client to see the Notable outcomes before committing.

steps.label: Reroll if needed
body: Use a Divine Orb to randomise both seed and name if the current roll does not fit your build.

steps.label: Desecrate (Undying Hate only)
body: Optionally use up to 4 Preserved Craniums to add Desecrated modifiers; this makes the jewel Unstable and raises destruction risk.

before: The small, notable, and keystone nodes in the chosen radius hold their original passive effects.
after: Those same nodes are Conquered and replaced with Kalguur or Abyssal versions decided by the seed and name.
compare.note: Socket placement and the seed/name together decide the entire result; a wrong socket or seed wastes the jewel.

sections.title: Build usage
intro: Timeless Jewels enable several distinct build shapes. Each row lists the fields you must get right and the most common mis-buy.
Because only one Historic jewel is allowed, pick the shape that matches your build's core need before spending currency.

builds.title: Keystone Enabler (Heroic Tragedy)
builds.description: Uses the leader name to convert an in-radius Keystone into a defensive conversion. Depends on name, not seed, for the Keystone; seed picks Notables. Cannot be replaced by a cheap version if you need the exact Keystone.

builds.title: Small Passive Scaling (Undying Hate)
builds.description: Every small passive in radius becomes +5 Tribute (and +3 attribute Tribute). Scales with how many small nodes you conquer. Cheap seeds can work if you only need Tribute bulk.

builds.title: Notable Transformation
builds.description: Seed decides Notables that scale with Tribute (Undying Hate) or become Kalguur notables (Heroic Tragedy). The exact Notables vary wildly by seed; verify in planner.

builds.title: Desecrated Modifier Build
builds.description: Adds 1-4 Desecrated modifiers via Preserved Cranium. Highest power but carries Unstable Desecration risk; most builds stop at 2-3 mods.

builds.title: High-budget Min-max
builds.description: Pays for a perfect seed plus 3-4 Desecrated mods. Requires verifying seed, name, socket, AND desecration outcome before committing.

sections.title: Alternatives
paragraphs: A normal Jewel (Magic/Rare) gives its own modifiers without conquering nodes; it is the alternative when you do not want to transform radius passives. Time-Lost Jewels also affect nodes in radius but are a different item with a different modifier pool - do not confuse them with Timeless Jewels.

Other Unique jewels (The Adorned, From Nothing, Controlled Metamorphosis, Megalomaniac, Voices) provide their own socket or tree mechanics and do not conquer radius passives the way a Timeless Jewel does.
If you only need a single Keystone that already exists on the tree, a Timeless Jewel's transformation may be unnecessary; reserve it for when you want a converted or themed Keystone and Notable set.
bullets: Normal / Magic / Rare jewel: own modifiers, no conquest.
Time-Lost Jewel: different item, different pool - not a Timeless Jewel.
Other Unique jewels: different mechanics, not radius conquest.

sections.title: Valuation: use, sell, or hold
marketNote: Prices reflect the Early Access 0.5.4 league on the PC trade site as of early August 2026 and move constantly; confirm the live number on poe.ninja before any large trade.

Value is driven by seed quality (rare, build-defining Notables), the desired leader/faction name, and - for Undying Hate - the number of Desecrated modifiers. A perfect 4-mod Undying Hate can reach mirror-tier prices.

entries.question: What is the difference between a Timeless Jewel and a Time-Lost Jewel?
summary: Players confuse the two because both affect radius nodes; they are separate item bases.
editorialAnalysis: A Timeless Jewel is a Unique Historic jewel that conquers and replaces radius passives with themed versions; a Time-Lost Jewel is a different base that modifies nodes in radius with its own pool. They are not interchangeable.
officialAnswer: Timeless and Time-Lost are distinct items; do not apply Time-Lost conclusions to Timeless Jewels.

entries.question: Why did my same-named Heroic Tragedy give different Notables?
summary: A player bought a jewel with the right leader name but the Notables were wrong for their build.
editorialAnalysis: The leader name decides the Keystone; the seed number decides the Notables. Two jewels with the same name but different seeds produce different Notables.
officialAnswer: Seed decides Notables, name decides Keystones - verify both before buying.

entries.question: Can my Undying Hate be destroyed by Desecration?
summary: Players ask whether Desecration can brick the jewel.
editorialAnalysis: Desecration makes Undying Hate Unstable. The official wording describes an increasing destruction probability with each Desecration; no fixed percentage is published. Risk rises with each use (up to 4).
officialAnswer: Desecration raises the chance of destruction; only an increasing probability is officially described, not a fixed number.

entries.question: Is the 0.4 Undying Hate keystone change important for my build?
summary: A video covered the 0.4 Tecrod Sacrifice of Blood change.
editorialAnalysis: Patch 0.4.0 changed Tecrod's Sacrifice of Blood to 1 Life/sec per 16 Life spent in the past 4 seconds and 20% more Life Cost of Skills (was 8s/8 Life, 50% more). Old 0.1/0.2 conclusions about this Keystone are invalid.
officialAnswer: Use only current 0.5.4 values for Undying Hate keystones.

problems.symptom: My Timeless Jewel did nothing when socketed
directAnswer: A Timeless Jewel only affects nodes inside its Very Large radius. If the socket's radius covers no useful nodes, you see little change. Also remember only one Historic jewel is allowed.
checks: Check which nodes fall inside the radius and confirm no other Historic jewel is already equipped.

problems.symptom: I bought the same name but got different Notables
directAnswer: The name decides the Keystone; the seed decides the Notables. A different seed means different Notables even with the same name.
checks: Verify the seed number in a planner before buying; do not rely on name alone.

directAnswer: Desecration makes the jewel Unstable and the chance of destruction increases with each use. No fixed percentage is published; only an increasing probability is officially described.
checks: Back up the tooltip, and consider stopping at 2-3 Desecrated mods.

problems.symptom: Old guides say different keystone values
directAnswer: Conclusions from 0.1 or 0.2 about Undying Hate keystones are invalid after the 0.4.0 change. Use current 0.5.4 client/planner data.
checks: Re-verify keystone values against the live client before building around them.
